lines.en: : Hey. Mind if I join you?
: Well, well, well. Look who finally decided to give me the time of day.
: I’m pretty sure we’ve already crossed over to the time of night, Haruka.
: Then that just goes to show you how long you’ve been avoiding me.
: I’m not intentionally avoiding you. I just-
: I know. I’m not hunting for an apology or anything like that.
: You were sort of a last minute addition to this trip in the first place, so it’s not like I’d been looking forward to spending time with you for weeks on end or whatever.
: Besides, you’ve got enough going on with Ami. If leaving me out of the equation helps you balance things out, so be it.
: I can wait a little longer.
: Bold claim for someone who gets lonely the second no one’s looking at her.
: It’s a little easier when the people I want to look at me aren’t in space.
: Your poor husband.
: Don’t bring him up right now. Let’s talk about you. How did things go with your potentially demonic niece? You guys were gone for a while.
: Pretty good actually...
: Apparently, she was already looking at me like some sort of father figure. And it was just me who was holding that back from turning into anything bigger.
: I’m not surprised, really. With the way that girl talks about you, I had a hard time ever believing you were just her uncle.
: Of course, the fact that she very openly called me out on being an unfaithful slut may have played a part in me thinking she might like you a little more than a standard relative. But I digress.
: And I digress because I am an unfaithful slut.
: But you’re my unfaithful slut and that is precisely why I keep you around.
: I’d be quite offended to hear that if it weren’t for the fact that being degraded turns me on.
: But I digress again.
: What gave it away?

: One of the many conversations I’ve overheard at the cafe where she talked about having your babies. Which isn’t really a thing someone should do with their father either. But hey, I’ve got some weird kinks too.
: You think things will get better from here on out?
: Better how?
: Like...do you think reevaluating your relationship with Ami will help you eventually find happiness outside of what your students keep beneath their skirts?
: Maybe. But it’s not really my happiness I’m concerned about. I just want Ami to stop blaming herself for not being able to break my concrete shoes off as I slowly descend to the ocean floor.
: Don’t you think that goes both ways, though?
: What do you mean?
: I mean...she knows you better than anyone, doesn’t she? Which means she probably wants you to stop blaming yourself for the things that are drowning her. You’re doing the same thing.
: But in my case, I’m actually making mistakes. And she’s-
: Making mistakes too. She’s only human, Sensei. And making mistakes is what humans do.
: Like, just look at us. Our entire relationship is a mistake. But it’s not like that’s stopping me from enjoying it while it lasts.

: Like, just look at me. I practically threw myself at you not long after we first met and I’m already spoken for. But you’re one of my best friends now, and that wouldn’t have happened without that mistake. You know?

: I know. But still...she’s just a girl. She shouldn’t have to be thinking about all of this depressing shit so early in her life. So all I want to do now is try and...save her a little bit of anguish.
: Is that really all you want to do, though?
: Is there something else you think I should want?
: I mean...you’re still kind of unemployed, aren’t you?
: Rin says it’s been aeons since you’ve shown up at school. And I doubt spending so much time alone is doing much for your mental health, so...don’t you want to change at least that?
: Silence speaks volumes sometimes, Sensei.
: You know...
: I think there was a time where I actually kind of enjoyed teaching. But, knowing me, I don’t really believe any of it was for the same reasons other people get into the field.

: Like...the girl who’s filling in for me right now. She seems to really love all of the girls in the class and she’s only known them a fraction of the time I have. It’s easy to tell that she, like...wants to make a difference.

: So even if she got into teaching for the wrong reasons, it’s the right ones that are keeping her around. And that’s...pretty obviously not how it was for me since you already know what I’m doing with some of those girls.
: Yeah, but you’ve neglected to tell me why you got into teaching in the first place. What do you mean by saying it wasn’t for the same reasons other people get into it?
: I mean...I can only guess how I was feeling back then.
: But I’m pretty sure it was to try and prevent anyone from winding up like me.
: I...don’t really get it. You decided to mentor people so...they wouldn’t wind up like you? Isn’t that kind of backwards?
: Maybe I worded that incorrectly. What I mean is more that...
: There are certain ways you’re meant to act in this world. And doing things to set yourself apart from others is generally discouraged.
: But there are some of us who really want to do things like that and can’t seem to figure out how.

: We want to fit in and we want to seem normal. But we’re products of the way we’re brought up and, a lot of the time, we never have the chance to understand what we’re meant to do in the first place.

: I think what I wanted is to take what I’ve learned and share that with people experiencing something similar. So they don’t wind up roaming through life confused or lost like I did for so long before just...giving up.
: Wow...
: I think that’s the most I’ve ever heard you say at once.
: Yeah, well...I’m sorry it all probably sounded like nonsense.
: Not at all. In fact, I think gaining this sort of...insight into your allegedly misguided mind explains a lot really.

: I’ve never thought you were normal or anything like that. Which might sound like an insult, but it’s really not. And I think that’s why people like Rin and I gravitate to you because we’re not normal either.
: Yeah but, in that sense, nobody is really normal. And yeah, Rin’s an orphan — but I’d wager you had a pretty standard upbringing. Am I right?
: More or less.
: I did well in school. I had parents who fed me and put a roof over my head. The whole nine yards. And I sure as hell never slept with any teachers like Sara did.

: But look at me now, Sensei. Like, sure- I’m a somewhat successful business owner. I’ve got a roof over my head and a car and a group of friends I can go camping with on random Sundays whenever I want.
: But I’m insanely lonely. I’m a borderline nymphomaniac. I send naked pictures of myself to teenage girls and pretend I never meant to.
: But I’m also a predator who will not only bend to your each and every desire, but eat out teenage girls on beaches and finger myself to fantasies about you fucking my friends’ daughters.
: And I do all of that with my “standard upbringing.” So maybe that’s less responsible for the way you are than you think. Just some food for thought.
: Fair point, Haruka.
: I can be pretty smart when I want to. Not just anyone can set their sights on opening a cafe when they’re a kid and then actually follow through with it.
: You’ve wanted that cafe since you were a kid?
: It was practically my dream.
: I remember this one project we had to do in school one year where we needed to come up with a whole-ass business proposal. You know — blueprints...logo...everything.
: And my pitch was basically Koi Cafe. Just, back then I think I called it Rainbow Cafe or...Sunflower Cafe or something like that. It was girly. That’s all I really remember.
: But, years later when I was less into pink and more into coffee, I rethought the base concept and landed on Koi instead.
: As in “love?”
: As in the fish, actually.
: Koi fish are linked to all sorts of symbolism because they’re beautiful and easy to, like...be poetic about, I guess. But to me, they’ve always stood for accomplishment. Or courage. Strength, even.
: And, I’m sure you’ve noticed this by now, but I’m kind of an overly sensitive piece of shit drama queen sometimes.
: So choosing a symbol for the qualities I lack seemed like a way for me to trick myself into believing I might actually have them, you know?
: I guess I never realized how much thought went into it. I always just saw it as some...normal cafe.
: It is! But it’s my normal cafe.
: It’s the symbol of all that hard work paying off. An actual, physical thing that embodies the...great accomplishment of a girl my age winning.
: I never won at much when I was younger, Sensei. But I also never really had time to win because I was thinking so much about the future.
: I don’t have to do that anymore because I like where I am. But, at the same time...
: It’s things like this that make me worry about you since you don’t have anything like that to remind you of all you’ve had to go through to get here.
: You had the school. You had your class. But now, you’re letting all of that drift away because you lost sight of why it was ever important to you in the first place.
: So maybe stop seeing it as a training ground for corrupting today’s youth and start seeing it as a place where you can connect with the people you want to connect with. Just like you used to.
: One thing I’ve learned from my time in the service industry is that everyone has problems, Sensei. And some people like talking about those problems way too much.
: But what that really means is that there’s always someone who will need what you have to offer.
: And for me, that’s coffee.
: It’s a place for people to relax or refuel to prepare themselves for the hell that lies outside of my doors.
: And for you, it’s...
: Actually...what subject do you even teach?
: All of them.
: All of them? Is that how they’re doing things over there now?
: It might just be a budget thing, but...I just want to say — I think that was one of the most helpful things you or...anyone else has ever said to me.
: Like I said, I can be pretty smart when I want to. You probably just forget that since I’m always hanging out with Maki and Sara.
: Haruka.
: Hm?
: I’m really proud of you.
: You really have done a lot to be proud of. And I’m glad you have something that serves as physical proof of that.
: Thank...you...
: No problem. But why do you look so embarrassed all of a sudden when you just spent the last ten minutes essentially giving yourself the same compliment?
: It’s different when it comes from someone else, obviously. Especially someone you look up to.
: Sure, but you only look up to me because I can get all of the girls that you can only dream of getting.
: There are other things too, you know!
: Like what?
: Like...the fact that you can withstand multiple apparent traumas when most people get taken out of commission by just one!
: Haruka, I was just stuck inside of my house for months. You shouldn’t look up to me just because I’m voluntarily stepping back out into the sun again.
: That was just one more thing! There’s also the part where...you’re caring! And cool!
: In fact, practically everyone looks up to you even though they probably shouldn’t!
: You’re right. They should be looking up to you instead.
: Ugh...no. That’s wrong too. And it’s not what I’m saying.
: What I mean is more like...how do I even put this?
: What I mean is that...it’s just kind of embarrassing hearing you say things like that since I never really...contemplated getting that sort of validation from you.
: It’s just surprising, that’s all.
: But...it makes me really happy.
: Almost happy enough to forget that you spent the first half of today hanging out with literally everyone else.
: Yeah...sorry about that.
: I’ll make sure to drop by the cafe again soon, though.
: Make sure it’s when I’m working...
: I can show you how it compares to my old blueprint.
Haruka pours some coffee into small paper cups that the two of us sip from for the next fifteen minutes or so while lazily gazing up at the stars.
You can see so many of them out here.
And for once, it almost doesn’t hurt to look at them.
Haruka rests her head on my shoulder, but not in the way that would make it seem like she wants me more than she actually does.
I think she’s just happy to be here beside me.
And I think that if I put my arm around her now that she’ll interpret it the same.
And so I do.
And so she does.
And we both close our eyes.
But when I open mine another ten minutes later after dozing, I notice she’s gone.
And so I must go as well.
Haruka’s affection has increased to [haruka_love]!
What now?
Haruka rests her head on my shoulder.
Several minutes later, she looks up at me- silently asking for something else.
But it’s something I can not give her here.
It wouldn’t feel right beneath the magpies.
Haruka’s affection has increased to [haruka_love]!
What should I do now?
